text: Before an engineer — or an AI agent — changes
production, it needs more than code.
It needs the incidents, decisions, dependencies, and runbooks surrounding that
change. Today, that context is scattered across repositories, Slack, and
postmortems. OrgMemory brings it together with its evidence — and,
through WebMCP, makes it available to an agent at the
moment it needs to act.
This authenticated page exposes OrgMemory through WebMCP — browser-native tools
that use the page's existing session and permissions.
The agent never receives a separate API credential.
It can only access what the signed-in user is allowed
to access. Let's see it work.
I'll ask it to restart the payments connection pool.
The most important tool here is get_orgmemory_briefing.
Instead of answering a general question, it evaluates an intended
action. Here, the agent says it plans to restart the
payments connection pool. OrgMemory returns a clear verdict: requires approval.
It surfaces two related incidents, the decision that capped worker
concurrency, and the blast radius — payments shares a Postgres
cluster with the ledger. It also returns the remembered first-response
procedure. Every claim includes a memory ID a person can
open and verify against its original evidence.
This briefing path is deterministic.
Running the same intent against the same organizational memory produces
the same verdict. A production control shouldn't change just because
a model phrased its answer differently.
The boundary is based on the intended action, not simply
the topic. A read-only investigation can proceed.
A potentially disruptive production action requires human approval.
OrgMemory doesn't approve its own recommendation.
Reads are permission-trimmed to the user's team scope.
Reporting an outcome only appends to the ledger.
And adding a fact to shared company memory requires a
proposal a human reviews. Capability is never treated as authorization.
Serving the briefing opens an entry in the outcome ledger.
After acting — from GitHub, PagerDuty, or another system —
the agent calls record_orgmemory_outcome with what it did and whether
it worked. Now the loop is complete: context served, action
taken, outcome observed. Over time, OrgMemory learns which company context
actually led to successful action.
OrgMemory gives every engineering change its full company context —
with evidence, permissions, and human control.
Through WebMCP, agents can check what matters before they act,
and report what happened afterward.
OrgMemory: put what your organization has learned to work.
